title: Microbes
examples: What is the difference between bacteria and viruses?
Can all microbes make us sick?
Where do we find useful microbes in nature?

explain.say: Today we are learning about tiny living things called microbes.
Bacteria are single-celled living organisms that reproduce quickly.
Viruses are much smaller than bacteria and need a host to live.

draw.text: Viruses: Need a host to live

explain.say: Fungi are a group that includes things like molds and mushrooms.
Some microbes are helpful, like those in our gut that help digestion.
Some microbes are harmful and can cause diseases in living things.

faq.q: Are all bacteria bad for us?
faq.a: No, many bacteria are helpful. They live in our bodies and help us digest food.

faq.q: How are viruses different from bacteria?
faq.a: Viruses are much smaller than bacteria. They cannot reproduce on their own and need a living cell to multiply.
asks: What is the main difference between viruses and bacteria?
Do viruses need help to live?

faq.q: What is the main difference between fungi and bacteria?
faq.a: Fungi are different from bacteria because they often grow in visible structures like mushrooms. Bacteria are single-celled organisms.

faq.q: Can we use microbes to make medicine?
faq.a: Yes, scientists use helpful microbes to produce antibiotics and other useful medicines.
asks: What is the medical use of bacteria?

faq.q: If I get sick, is it always a microbe?
faq.a: Most common sicknesses are caused by microbes, but sometimes other things can make us ill too.
asks: Is everything that makes me sick a microbe?

facts: Bacteria reproduce by dividing into two identical cells.
Viruses require a living host cell to carry out their life cycle.
Fungi include organisms like yeasts, molds, and mushrooms.
Some bacteria are essential for breaking down waste in nature.

quiz.say: A single-celled organism that can live on its own is:
quiz.why: Bacteria are true cells and can reproduce by themselves.

wrong.1: Viruses cannot reproduce on their own; they need a host cell.
wrong.2: Fungi are usually more complex than single-celled bacteria.
wrong.3: Molds are a type of fungus, not the general category of single-celled life.

quiz.say: Which microbe group includes items like bread mold?
quiz.why: Molds are a common example of the fungal kingdom.

wrong.0: Bacteria are prokaryotic cells, different from fungi.
wrong.1: Viruses are not classified as fungi.
wrong.2: Protists are a different group of organisms not covered here.

quiz.say: If a microbe needs a living cell to multiply, it is likely a:
quiz.show: Needs a host cell to multiply:
quiz.why: This describes the obligate nature of viral replication.

wrong.1: Bacteria can reproduce independently without a host cell.
wrong.2: Fungi can grow and reproduce on their own substrates.
wrong.3: Yeast is a type of fungus that grows independently.
